title: Replace an electric toothbrush's worn brush head with the new one from its pack
instruction: Replace the electric toothbrush's worn brush head with the new one from its pack, and put the worn one in the bin. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Electric toothbrush heads are replaced about every three months: the new head has to come out of its pack and go on in place of the worn one. It is a small everyday chore that people with the use of only one hand need help with.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A dark grey granite bathroom counter top 1 cm thick, from 17 to 48 cm forward and from 25 cm right to 20 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) Lying on its back on the counter, an electric toothbrush (140 g): a white ABS handle 17 cm long and 2.6 cm across with a flat back, a blue band and a blue power button, its steel drive shaft (4.4 mm across, 2.4 cm long) pointing forward; the handle's middle is 28 cm forward, 0.5 cm right of the centre line. (3) On the shaft, a worn round brush head (polypropylene with nylon bristles, 5 g, 8.1 cm long): a dark blue collar 1.6 cm across, a white neck 1.1 cm across and 5.2 cm long and a round head 1.9 cm across with yellowed, splayed bristles facing up. It is a push fit on the shaft. (4) A new brush head, the same with white and blue bristles, shut in its reclosable clear PET clamshell (0.35 mm PET, 12 g: tray 6 g, lid 6 g) lying flat on the counter from 19 to 32 cm forward, centred 8.5 cm right of the centre line. The tray is 13 x 6.4 cm and 1.2 cm deep, lined with a blue printed card; its front 3 cm is a raised, ribbed thumb rest. The head lies in it on two cradles, its base 3.4 cm behind the tray's front, neck pointing forward. The lid covers the tray behind the thumb rest (10 x 6.4 cm), with a bubble 2.9 cm wide and 3.6 cm high over the head; it is hinged along the tray's right-hand edge by a moulded living hinge, and two press studs along its left-hand edge, 7.6 cm apart, snap it shut. (5) A white plastic pedal bin 9 cm across and 8.5 cm tall, 41.5 cm forward and 19 cm right of the centre line, fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The clamshell's press studs hold its lid shut until it is turned about its hinge with 0.18 N m (3.2 N at the studs, 5.6 cm from the hinge); once it has opened 1.5 degrees the studs are out and the moulded hinge swings the lid open to its 120-degree stop. Pushed back to within 0.8 degrees of shut, the studs catch again. A brush head slides along the shaft only when pushed or pulled with more than about 3 N (a push fit) and stays where it is left; pulled out past the shaft's end (2.8 cm) it is off. A head whose collar is pushed onto the free shaft's end (within 1 cm of its axis and 15 degrees of its line) catches on it, and it is all the way on when its base is within 3 mm of the shaft's base. All judged at the end of the trial, on live states: 1.0: the new head all the way on, the worn head in the bin (its base within 4 cm of the bin's axis, between its floor and rim) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the same with an arm not back; 0.5: the new head all the way on; 0.25: the pack open (studs out, lid at least 60 degrees open) and the worn head off the shaft; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the toothbrush, both heads, the tray and the lid still. In a real trial: the new head is all the way on when it has clicked down and the gap between its collar and the handle is under 3 mm (ruler); the worn head must lie in the bin (look in); the pack is open when its lid is off both studs and stands at least 60 degrees open (video or protractor); the arms are checked against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Push the worn head back onto the shaft, put the new head back on the tray's cradles, snap the clamshell shut and lay it and the toothbrush back in their places.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Real sizes and masses; the clamshell's PET walls are modelled 2-4 mm thick (real 0.35 mm) at its real 12 g. Simplified: the press studs are a capped detent on the lid's hinge (0.18 N m, free past 1.5 degrees) and the moulded hinge a weak spring, not snap geometry; each head's push fit is a joint that slides above about 3 N; heads don't collide with the handle, which has a flat back. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
